messages:
alex: Heads-up — planning a focused staging run to validate quota/rate-limit enforcement (per-key, per-org, and burst controls). Goal: prove we can't accidentally route around org quotas via cache sharding or token-bucket edge cases. Wanted to sync on schedule + test plan.

mira: +1. Do we have a specific harness? k6 or locust? also: which staging cluster (staging-a vs staging-b) — want to avoid overlapping with the nightly perf soak.

alex: k6 for the generator (lighter, easier in CI). staging-b is preferred (less noisy). plan: 3 phases — ramp (5m), steady soak (30m), chaotic spikes (10m). We'll run with two identity modes: api_key-only and org-scoped tokens.

devon: Re: attack surface: make sure rate-limiter lookup order is tested. We recently changed enforcement to check per-key token first, then org aggregate. If people use shared api_keys that map to many orgs, the path could undercount org traffic. I'll add control flags to force per-org-only mode for the run.

sam: For telemetry, I'll create a dashboard with these panels: qps by api_key, qps by org_id, 429-rate by route, token-bucket-occupancy (histogram), latency p50/p95/p99, and rejected-by-rule tag. Also add a log sample panel for "rate_limiter_decision" events.

alex: Nice. Also add a panel that shows redis key cardinality for token buckets and cache hit/miss rates — we want to detect sharding that creates one token bucket per request pattern.

mira: Can someone paste the k6 snippet (simple) so I can add to CI? want to validate headers and rate of unique api_key values.\
devon: Sure — quick k6 test (minimal):
```js
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';

export let options = { vus: 200, duration: '25m' };

const ORG_IDS = ['org-A','org-B','org-C'];
const API_KEYS = Array.from({length: 100}, (_,i) => `test-key-${i}`);

export default function () {
  let headers = { Authorization: `Bearer ${API_KEYS[Math.floor(Math.random()*API_KEYS.length)]}`, 'X-Org-ID': ORG_IDS[Math.floor(Math.random()*ORG_IDS.length)] };
  http.post('https://staging-b.api.redwood/api/v1/generate', JSON.stringify({prompt: 'fuzz'}), { headers });
  sleep(0.1);
}
```

devon: For the spikes phase we'll run short bursts with 2000 VUs for 1m against single org to validate burst caps.

sam: I'll add alerts on staging dashboards: if 429 rate > 0.5% for more than 2m (during steady) or if token-bucket-occupancy < 10% for >1m (indicates we drained buckets).

alex: Ops question: do we want to enable the experimental "per-org-strict" path (flag) that bypasses per-key optimizations? If yes, toggle it only on staging-b and record responses.

devon: I added a feature-flag toggle in staging console under /flags/rate_limiter_per_org_strict. I'll flip it for the run. Be aware it changes Redis key shapes: single org key vs api_key+org composite.

mira: Who can run the flip and the k6 job? I can kick off k6 but need someone with flag perms to change it when we move to spike phase.

sam: I can handle dashboards and alerting. devon — please flip at t+10m and flip back at end. I'll annotate graphs.

devon: Will do. ops-bot: please post a deploy window for staging-b and block scheduled infra jobs for the next 1.5h.

ops-bot: Notice: maintenance window requested for staging-b at 2026-02-12T03:00Z — blocking auto-scheduled infra jobs for 90 minutes.

alex: Quick checklist before we run: (1) k6 script uploaded to ci/test-assets, (2) dashboards ready, (3) flag set to per-key mode initially, (4) data capture (logs + traces) enabled for rate_limiter_decision, (5) ops window set. Anything else?

sam: Add a small traffic pattern that uses many semi-unique api keys (simulate thousands) to catch cardinality blowups. Use a TTL inspector on redis to ensure tokens expire.

devon: One more gotcha: CDN + edge caching can hide origin QPS. Ensure we target token-validation route that hits origin (bypass CDN) or add cache-control: no-cache header. I'll add that to the k6 request.

mira: Running now — starting ramp. tagging @devon @sam for the flag flip at +10m.

alex: Thanks — I'll watch the 429s and per-org panel. If we see orgs with near-zero 429 but per-key is saturated, that's a red flag.

sam: Graphs: initial 200 VUs ramp looks clean. p95 steady at ~110ms. token-bucket-occupancy trending down to ~35% for org-A.

devon: Flipping flag to per_org_strict now.

deploy-bot: Flag change applied: /flags/rate_limiter_per_org_strict = true by devon at 1759876600.

mira: Spike phase starting — running 2k VUs for 60s against org-A.

sam: Observability: sudden jump in redis key counts + 429 spike to 7% for org-A, per-key 429 spread unevenly. Looks like composite keys created too many buckets and org aggregate enforcement delayed.

alex: Hmm — that's the exact behavior we feared. devon, did the strict flag switch the enforcement order? I thought strict forces org-first.

devon: It did, but we discovered a race where request routing goes to different workers that have different local caches of bucket state; stitching the aggregate requires a short redis increment + read; under high concurrency we observed a window where per-key local token allowed the request but org counter hadn't caught up.

mira: Any mitigation ideas? short-term for prod: increase org burst capacity or tighten worker-side local allowance and favor org check synchronously. Long-term: single global rendezvous for org-buckets or consistent hashing to ensure same worker handles orgs.

devon: I've prototyped a cheap fix: on high concurrency for orgs with active spike, fall back to synchronous org-consensus mode (extra redis increment+check). I'll bake it into runtime and run again in a smaller spike to validate.

sam: Logging shows many "decision=allow local_cache=true org_seen=false" events. I'll export a sample set for postmortem.

alex: Great work. Let's stop the job, collect traces, and schedule a small follow-up to decide prod rollout strategy. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

mira: Stopping k6. Uploading artifacts (k6 summary + traces) to the run ticket.

devon: Filed a follow-up RFC: "avoid-org-enforcement-race" and attached runtime patch.

sam: Artifacts uploaded. I'll open a short postmortem template and include the dashboards + logs.

alex: Closing the loop — we validated the issue, have a mitigation plan, and collected telemetry. Good run.
